title: Commissary Adolf Ebers (Eberschildt) in Moscow, 1662-1666 (Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica 3/b/602): key of the two-digit German letter code rebuilt from the contemporary glosses and validated

documents.shelfmark: Stockholm, Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica, SE/RA/2113/2113.1/3/b/602 (Kommissarien Adolf Ehbers (Eberschildt), Moskva, 1662-1666), images R0003225_00106 and R0003225_00108
documents.route: Adolf Ebers (Swedish commissary in Moscow) -> Charles XI (the Regency)

plaintext.source: A contemporary German decipherment is written above every code run on the pages checked.

transcription.source: Riksarkivet IIIF, images 106 and 108 at 3000 px (public viewer, no login)
transcription.notes: Training part of the key: 53 glossed words (cipher groups with the gloss above them). Image 108 is a second copy of the letter of image 106. The clear German text is not transcribed.

documents.shelfmark: Stockholm, Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica, SE/RA/2113/2113.1/3/b/602, image R0003225_00138, left page

plaintext.source: A contemporary German decipherment is written above every code run.

transcription.notes: Held-out part of the key test: the first 160 cipher groups, transcribed after the key was frozen, then the gloss read; 5 groups cut in the binding.

system.summary: German letter substitution with homophones, two-digit groups 15-95 separated by dots, mixed with clear German; a few letters have two numbers (a 15/77, e 22/81, f 24/25, n 45/89, o 47/90, s 94/53, t 95/55) and doubled letters have their own numbers (ll 42, mm 44, ss 54). Arabic numerals are written in clear. 46 seen once, unresolved.

prior_solution.where: The German glosses written over the code runs at the time are a decipherment, on every page checked (ours: 81, 98R, 101, 102R, 103, 106, 108, 124, 133, 138, 143; Daniel Bourdeau's leads review n09 of 6 Nov 2026: 106, 108, 112, 114, 119, 121, 138, 140, 145, 160), so the content is not new. No printed key or edition found (leads review n09: nothing on DECODE, at Cryptiana or in Lasry's lists); no target, branch or PR for Ebers or R0003225 in this repository (GitHub API, 10 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau's Riksarkivet sweep found the volume and his leads review n09 (6 Nov 2026) vetted it as lead 2315 ('read': glossed throughout). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Images 106 and 108: 53 glossed words (cipher groups with the gloss over them) read from the 3000 px IIIF images.
Key of 31 codes learned from the glossed words of images 106 and 108 only; frozen by SHA-256 with the protocol before the held-out part was transcribed.

One measurement on image 138 (first 160 groups, transcribed after the freeze, gloss read after the numbers): 0.909 of characters against 0.047 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (mean 0.021); margin 0.862; thresholds >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30, fixed in advance.

Gloss inventory on images 81, 98R, 101, 102R, 103, 106, 108, 124, 133, 138 and 143: a gloss over every run, no bare passage found (agrees with leads review n09). 108 is a second copy of 106; 143 repeats the letter of 138; the foot of 103/104 holds copies.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the contemporary interlinear decipherment (glosses) of images 106 and 108 and validated once on image 138. The content is the glosses' (existing); the key is the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol and key hashed before the held-out part was transcribed; one measurement on image 138 (160 groups, 165 decoded positions): 0.909 of characters vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.047 (mean 0.021), margin 0.862. Threshold fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30. Later additions 53 = s and 55 = t are derived after the measurement and not tested; 46 unresolved.

texts.label: Image 138, left page: the 160 held-out cipher groups with the contemporary gloss
texts.note: The cipher runs of the measured portion, broken by clear German that is not transcribed, so a sequence of phrases rather than a running text: our decode with key.tsv beside the gloss written at the time. The gloss is the reading of the time.
texts.summary: Ebers reports that something has been taken into consideration and decided here: envoys are to go to Poland for the boundary commission, with the voivodes at Smolensk, to treat with the Poles; Marselis and Nashchokin are named, and someone is in favour ('in gnade').

reading_review.note: decode read against the contemporary gloss as German phrases; agrees except spellings (kluch/klug, gesanten/gesandten, naschokin/naskokin) and 5 groups cut in the binding; phrases only, the clear text between the runs not transcribed; one reader

outcome.notes: The letters were deciphered at the time (interlinear glosses on every page checked), so we claim no reading and no solution; what is new is the key as a reusable table, validated on a held-out page. Lead 2316 (Lilienthal, Diplomatica Muscovitica 1/36/82) uses a different code (a homophonic letter substitution in six 2-3 digit series, not a nomenclator); its key is in target lilienthal1665 (PR #384).
